## Purpose 
Implicit treatment of 1M rain evaporation and snow sublimation/deposition

Extends the existing implicit 1M microphysics path (previously limited to cloud liquid/ice condensation) to also cover rain evaporation and snow sublimation/deposition.

- Parameter splitting (`create_parameters.jl`, `Parameters.jl`): when `implicit_microphysics: true`, `rain_condensation_evaporation` and `snow_deposition_sublimation` are moved from the bulk CM BMT call into the implicit parameter set, so a second CM BMT call isolates their tendencies into `ᶜmp_tendency_implicit.dq_rai_dt` / `dq_sno_dt` per Newton iterate.

- Tendency wiring (`tendency.jl`): `ᶜmp_tendency_implicit.dq_rai_dt` and `dq_sno_dt` are added to the `ρq_rai` and `ρq_sno` tendency accumulation (grid-mean and EDMF updrafts). Previously only `dq_lcl_dt`/`dq_icl_dt` were picked up from the implicit cache.

- Jacobian (manual_sparse_jacobian.jl):
  - Rain: `∂rate/∂q_rai ≈ tend/q_rai` when `tend < 0`; zero otherwise.
  - Snow sublimation: `tend/q_sno` when `tend < 0`.
  - Snow deposition: `−C` where `C = 4πn₀G/(ρλ²)·vent` is the ventilation-integral prefactor of `S` in `rate = C·S`, computed without dividing by `S` and therefore well-defined even when grid-mean `S ≤ 0` (SGS quadrature regime).

body:
Follow-up to #4664: makes the `TRMM_LBA` radiation GPU-compatible, so a full `TRMM_LBA` simulation runs on a GPU space.

`APL.TRMM_LBA_radiation` is a 2D (time × height) `Interpolations.jl` interpolant that is not isbits. It was held by `RadiationTRMM_LBA`, which lives in the `AtmosModel`, and the `AtmosModel` is captured whole into device kernels (for example `update_surface_conditions!`), so a `TRMM_LBA` run crashed at initialization on a GPU space with a non-isbits kernel argument.

`RadiationTRMM_LBA` becomes an isbits marker and the profile moves into the radiation cache. The radiative-cooling tendency resolves the time coordinate on the host into the height profile at `t`, then interpolates in height on the device with a `ClimaInterpolations.Interpolation1D.Interpolate1D` over `SVector` knots. Only the small height-profile `SVector`, not the full 36 × 33 table, enters the kernel, so the kernel-parameter footprint stays small and portable across GPUs. 

All devices share one path, so the CPU and GPU evaluations cannot diverge. CPU results change at the level of rounding.

`FileHeatFluxes` also holds a time interpolant, which is evaluated on the host. It is not exercised on a GPU here.
title: fix(radiation): make the TRMM_LBA radiation GPU-compatible

body:
This PR fixes two bugs in `ClimaAtmos.AtmosphericProfilesLibrary` that carried over from the standalone package in #4954.

`GATE_III_dqtdt` applied `q = r / (1 + r)` to the mixing ratio tendency itself instead of converting the tendency. It now uses `dq/dt = (dr/dt) / (1 + r)²` with the mixing ratio of the initial profile, so the tendency is up to 3.3% smaller. No ClimaAtmos setup uses this profile.

Changes
- Fix the GATE III moisture forcing conversion
- Return the profile's float type from `Bomex_dTdt`, `GATE_III_dTdt`, and `GATE_III_dqtdt`, which computed in Float64 for Float32 runs
- Add reference values for every case at table knots, between knots, at the edges of piecewise definitions, and beyond the data
- Check that each profile returns the float type it is built with

Float32 BOMEX output changes at the rounding level.
title: Fix the GATE III moisture forcing and the Bomex Float32 cooling

This reduces compile time as mutable structs are heap-allocated. As such, closures and containers that capture them hold a pointer instead of an inline copy. See https://buildkite.com/clima/climacoupler-time-to-first-step/builds/50#_ which use this branch and improve time to first step by 15%. Note that it was done on Julia 1.11.

This is the same kind of change made in https://github.com/CliMA/ClimaLand.jl/pull/1906.
title: Make AtmosCache and Jacobian mutable
